messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Elevated 504/502 gateway errors observed for private VPC inference-gw (eu-west-1). Error rate spiked at 07:12 UTC. Affected customers: several private deployments on dedicated subnets. Pager: #oncall. Runbook: <https://redwood/internal/runbooks/vpc-egress|vpc-egress-triage>.

sara-oncall: oncall here, acked. paging @ajay-net and @mike-infra. I'll start collecting impact and will coordinate mitigations.

ajay-net: jumping in. seeing abrupt jump in NAT port utilization on the NAT gateway tied to subnet-prod-a. CloudWatch: ephemeral-port-usage ~ 99.7% for nat-0123abcd. Also seeing increased conntrack ESTABLISHED count on the NAT instance (we have a fallback nat instance for some subnets).

ajay-net: snippets: ```
# conntrack -S
2576260 usec-cpu, found 257436 sockets
ipv4 entries 131072, ipv6 entries 0, hashsize 32768
```

ajay-net: and CloudWatch link: <https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/graphs?region=eu-west-1|nat-ports-graph> (spike at 07:11). Hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion from one or two noisy customers + asymmetric SNAT mapping across peering path.

mike-infra: I'm checking TGW and route tables. No recent infra deploys in eu-west-1 in the last hour per deploy bot. Also checking security group change history.

mike-infra: security group audit: recent rollout added an egress restriction to groups used by inference-gw that limits outbound port range to 1024-32767 for some instances — that's narrower than typical ephemeral range (32768-61000). If the instance tries to open >32767 outbound, packets get refused and retries cause more sockets -> weird failure patterns. I'm still validating.

lina-cs: clients reporting timeouts on private endpoints; one customer (acme-fin) opened a support case referencing 504s for long requests. Can we get an immediate mitigation for customers with private infra?

ajay-net: mitigation options: 1) create additional NAT gateway(s) and split subnets to spread port space; 2) adjust security group egress rules to allow full ephemeral range (recommended); 3) put heavy customers on dedicated egress path (dedicated NAT or dedicated TGW attachment). Quickest: update SG egress to allow full 1024-65535 range for affected groups.

mike-infra: I'm going to rollback the recent SG change ASAP for the groups tagged inference:private. Command: ```
# aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e --protocol tcp --port 32768-65535 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```

mike-infra: applied to sg-0a1b2c3d4e and sg-1b2c3d4e5f. Replacing rules now. Please monitor.

ajay-net: splitting outbound to extra NAT gateway for prod-a subnets (nat-0456efgh). I'll add a route replacement to route table rtb-0a11bb22 to the new NAT for half the private subnets. Executing: ```
# aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a11bb22 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0456efgh
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollback: inference-gateway v2 rollback to v2.14 triggered by deploy-control (reason: elevated client retries). Canary percent set to 0%.

sara-oncall: monitoring metrics now. Any signs of error-rate drop? Lina, can you update acme-fin that we're actively triaging and attempting mitigation (SG rollback + NAT split)? Suggest posting temporary workaround: use hosted API or route through Dedicated for urgent traffic.

lina-cs: messaging sent to acme-fin and a small set of affected customers. Notified them of mitigation steps. They asked for ETA.

ajay-net: after SG update and route split, I'm seeing conntrack entries steady and NAT port utilization drop to ~70% on the old gw and ~30% on the new. Visible improvement in 2min.

ajay-net: tcpdump from a NAT instance (snip): ```
10:14:32.123456 IP 10.0.2.45.52000 > 13.225.33.1.443: Flags [S], seq 123456789, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 1234 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
# lots of SYN retries hitting RST/ICMP due to SG egress policy earlier
```

mike-infra: confirmation: after rolling back the restrictive SG rule we added in the last change, outbound port acceptance rates normalized. Root cause: a mistaken narrower egress range deployed during a security hardening patch. We'll open a postmortem for why the rollout lacked canary checks for ephemeral ranges.

lina-cs: customers updated. Acme-fin confirmed reduced errors on their side. They asked for a write-up of remediation and a timeline for a permanent fix.

sara-oncall: quick handoff: I'll escalate to morning shift (@dave-sre) to follow up with permanent remediation (audit of SG automation and adding a check to the infra CI to prevent ephemeral-range narrowing). Logging incident as P2.

dave-sre: taking over. Noted mitigations: SG rollback and NAT split. Next steps: revert the security hardening change in infra-as-code, add a preflight in terraform plan to validate ephemeral ranges, and open a pricing/cost ticket to evaluate permanent dedicated egress for heavy customers.

sara-oncall: thanks team. marking the alert as acknowledged and moving to monitoring for 30m. If any regression, page oncall immediately. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Alert cleared in monitoring (rule: vpc-egress-504-rate) at 07:48 UTC.

dave-sre: I'll draft the incident summary and link to tickets. Handoff complete.

lina-cs: closing the customer communication loop. They appreciated the rapid response. :white_check_mark:
